newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Wheat mixed, maize down in hectic Budapest market.
newsitem.headline: Wheat mixed, maize down in hectic Budapest market.

text.p: Wheat futures were mixed and maize eased on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Wednesday, but no clear trend emerged after rather hectic trading, dealers said.

"At the beginning of trade, milling wheat futures continued Tuesday's rise but they reached a point when both physical and speculative selling became dominant, bringing prices down," said Sandor Torok of Agrokont.
Milling wheat rose 400 forints per tonne for May to 25,300, tradeless July remained flat at 21,000 forints, while positions from August to March 1998 finished 40 to 400 forints lower.
August closed at 21,920 forints, down 40, September dropped 400 forints to 22,090, October ended at 22,700, down 200, December lost 230 forints to 23,670 while March 1998 closed at 24,900, down 200.
Torok said the lack of fundamental change and significant price movements on international markets pointed to stagnating wheat prices on the BCE.
Old (1996) crop maize prices started a slow correction in balanced trade, with May easing 50 forints to 18,550 and July losing 110 to end at 17,700.
New (1997) crop maize dropped 400 forints to 18,600 for October and 90 forints to 18,900 for November and remained flat for December at 19,150 but turnover was insignificant for these months.
Torok said maize prices were also unlikely to produce spectacular changes over the next few days.
Feed barley dropped for July to October positions, mainly in response to easing milling wheat prices. August, the only traded month, dropped 400 forints to 18,290.

Total grains turnover rose for the fourth consecutive day to 359 million forints or 851 contracts compared with Tuesday's 308 million forints. Milling wheat and maize accounted for most turnover with 466 and 340 contracts respectively.
